quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: You do not have to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights if it is on a private road.
questions.explanation: You must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and its stop arm out. This rule applies on both public and private roads.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway:

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
There is no need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear. Always use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: If a driver sees an animal on the roadway:

options.text: Pass the animal as close as possible.

questions.explanation: Be very cautious when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly to avoid startling or scaring it.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light is used at dangerous intersections. Treat it the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: Drivers cannot pass from either side of a ____ centerline.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no traffic from either direction is allowed to cross it to pass.

questions.question: When you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and change lanes if possible so you do not drive next to the emergency vehicle.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and drive at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes if possible so you do not drive next to the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes if you can. If you cannot change lanes safely or there is only one lane, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much space as possible. Always slow down and be ready to stop near an emergency scene.

questions.question: It is against the law to drive alongside a motorcycle in the same lane.
questions.explanation: Never share a lane with a motorcycle, even if there appears to be enough room. Motorcycles need a full lane width to move safely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road joins from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is ahead and a road joins from the right.

questions.question: If you have a tire blowout:

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not use your brakes right away.
Slow down gradually and pull off the road.

questions.explanation: During a tire blowout, remove your foot from the gas pedal and do not brake immediately. Slow down gradually, then gently brake and pull off the road.

questions.question: On long trips, you can prevent drowsiness by:

options.text: Moving your eyes from side to side while driving.

questions.explanation: Stop regularly on long trips to rest and stretch, even if you do not feel tired. This helps prevent drowsiness.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: You must stop immediately and back up.
Drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange. They warn you that work is happening on or near the road. Drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: If you stop on the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on emergency flashers and low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on emergency flashers and low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: When you stop on the road at night, use your emergency flashers and keep your low beam headlights on. This makes sure other drivers can clearly see your vehicle.

questions.question: Your speed does not affect how far your vehicle travels after you brake.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop. Stay far behind other vehicles, especially on highways.

questions.question: If you are driving slowly and traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. If traffic backs up behind you on a two-lane road, pull off and let other vehicles pass. Only drive much slower than the speed limit when weather or road conditions require it.

questions.question: When approaching a roundabout, what should you always do?
questions.explanation: Slow down when you approach a roundabout. Roundabouts are designed for low speeds. If no other vehicles or people are in the roundabout, you may not need to stop completely.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Letting the car run in the driveway.

questions.explanation: Every time you brake suddenly, you use fuel to speed back up. If you look ahead and slow down gradually or change lanes, you avoid sudden braking. This saves gas.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.explanation: The larger the vehicle, the larger its blind spots. Big trucks and SUVs have areas behind them that cannot be seen in mirrors.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow X on a lane control signal mean?

options.text: The signal will soon turn to a red X.
The signal will soon turn to a green arrow.
You may only use this lane to turn left.
You may drive slowly in this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may only use this lane to turn left.
questions.explanation: Lane control signals show which lanes are open or closed. They change throughout the day. A flashing yellow X means you can only use that lane for a left turn.

questions.question: Before backing up your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check behind your vehicle before getting in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind your vehicle before getting in.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before you get in. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat.

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk when you see children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross safely. Always be alert for children when driving through intersections or turning.

questions.question: Fog makes it hard to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road and objects better.

questions.explanation: Fog reduces how far you can see. Drive carefully and slowly. Do not use high beams. Low beams work better in fog to light up the road and objects ahead.

questions.question: When you want to turn right, where should your car be?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Before a right turn, move to the right side of the road. Do not cut across other lanes.

questions.question: What shape and color is a slow-moving vehicle sign?
questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle sign is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this sign travel at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: What do yellow-green signs indicate?
questions.explanation: Yellow-green signs warn about pedestrians, bicycles, and school zones. Drive extra carefully around these signs.

questions.question: If your wheels drop onto the road shoulder, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.
Stop your car at the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, reduce your speed without braking. Turn carefully back onto the road. Watch for nearby traffic.

questions.question: You are on a multilane divided highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Slow down, move to make a clear path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to make a clear path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights, slow down and make a clear path for the emergency vehicle. Stop and wait. Do not try to outrun it.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk and on overcast days. Use low beams when 1,000 feet from an oncoming vehicle or 500 feet behind another vehicle. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn others.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance lets you react to problems without sudden braking. This helps prevent vehicles behind you from crashing into you.

questions.question: When parallel parking, your car should be within ____ of the curb.
questions.explanation: Park no more than 12 inches from the curb. Always park where drivers can see your vehicle from both directions.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a divided highway is ahead. The road splits into two one-way roadways with a median between them. Stay to the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow background. They warn drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign means the divided highway is ending.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They prepare drivers for road hazards ahead. This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming. Be ready to stop for a red light or watch for cross traffic.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus unloading children, what should you do?

options.text: Do not proceed until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm extended and lights flashing, watch for children walking along the road. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so poorly that they may appear drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
They are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so poorly that they may appear drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they look drunk. Opening a window, turning up the radio, or drinking coffee is not enough to make a drowsy driver stay alert.

questions.question: You come to an intersection with a flashing red light. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe to do so.
Stop only if other cars are also approaching the intersection.
Stop only if other cars are already within the intersection.
Slow down and be prepared to stop, if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop, let other traffic pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes or merging into traffic is:

options.text: Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: When changing lanes, check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder toward the next lane. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield the right-of-way to:

options.text: Other drivers who are already in the intersection.
Pedestrians who are already in the intersection.

questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic. Also yield to pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: What does an arrow painted on the road mean?

options.text: Drivers in the proper lane may make the movement indicated by the arrow if they choose to.
Drivers in the proper lane must make the movement indicated by the arrow, but only if traffic lights are not working.
Drivers in the proper lane must always come to a complete stop before making the movement indicated by the arrow.
Drivers in the proper lane must make the movement indicated by the arrow while following traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers in the proper lane must make the movement indicated by the arrow while following traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow painted on the road tells drivers in that lane they must make the movement shown by the arrow. Always follow traffic signs and signals before proceeding in the direction indicated by the arrow.

questions.question: Your vehicle takes longer to stop when stopping:

options.text: On a wet or icy road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Stopping distances increase on wet or icy roads. They also increase on loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: What does this road sign indicate?

options.text: The maximum safe speed for a residential area.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway entrance.
The maximum safe speed for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the safe speed limit for a highway exit. In this example, the safe speed is 30 mph.
